title: Choose the look for Rândul
question: The roll picked Market Price Cards. Keep it, take another, or roll again. You're choosing the dashboard shop owners use every day.

options.label: Market Price Cards
options.lineage: day-glo price cards on market stalls and shop counters
options.thesis: Prices and minutes are the loudest thing on screen, set like a stall's hand-cut price cards.
options.viewport: Green top bar with the shop name, then hairline-ruled service rows, each ending in an orange price tag with big condensed numerals and the minutes under it.
options.risk: Day-glo orange shouts; it must stay on prices and the main button only, or the dashboard turns into a discount aisle.

raised.raise: Hairline-ruled rows instead of shadowed cards, so a phone shows a whole menu at once.
One fixed state vocabulary (open, closed, day off, hidden) drawn the same way on every screen.
Hierarchy by scale contrast: huge price numerals, small quiet labels, no boxes to say what matters.
Nothing labeled twice: the price tag replaces the word Price.
On phones, the one next setup step stays pinned at the bottom of the screen.

options.label: Shop Window Lettering
options.lineage: signwriters' gold-leaf lettering and door hours plates
options.thesis: The dashboard reads like the shop's own front door: name in the fascia, hours on the glass.
options.viewport: Oxblood fascia bar with the shop name in gold, then the week laid out as a door hours plate above the service list.
options.risk: Gold on oxblood reads barbershop heritage, the familiar costume of this category, and suits a dentist less well.

options.label: Ticket Coupons
options.thesis: Every booking is a coupon that gets stamped: booked, done, or cancelled, never deleted.
options.viewport: Navy header, services as coupon rows with tabbed heads, the time and price struck in carbon purple.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with bookings and their states; loses on audience, because a corner shop is not air travel.
options.risk: A travel costume on a haircut once the novelty wears off.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: The week as a line map, shifts as stations.
options.case: Loses both: owners don't think of their week as a network.
options.risk: A map where a list is clearer.
options.kept: One fixed state vocabulary across every screen.

options.label: High-Density Web
options.thesis: Pack the whole shop on one screen.
options.viewport: A mosaic of small ruled modules.
options.case: Loses both: too dense for owners who aren't technical.
options.kept: Hairline rules instead of shadowed cards.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: Loses both: shops don't care about type axes.
options.risk: A design toy, not a tool.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.viewport: A black field with a catalog number.
options.case: Loses both: codes hide what owners need to read.
options.risk: Unreadable for the people using it.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.viewport: One full-screen item, actions on the right.
options.case: Loses both: setup is a list of tasks, not a feed.
options.risk: Hides the rest of the shop.
options.kept: The one next step stays in view on phones.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What booking apps usually ship, executed with full care.
canonCard.viewport: White screen, sidebar, services as rounded cards with a purple button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other booking app by design.
